why: In an old-style class's constructor `class(s, name)` makes the object of the class (doc 'class'; `mfilename` there is the class's own name, doc 'mfilename'), whatever the name is written as: `tidy(obj)` after `obj = class(s, mfilename)` in `@Gizmo/Gizmo.m`, and after `obj = class(s, "Nut")` in `@Nut/Nut.m`, is the class's method.
